title: regional-fallback-burn-in-stabilizer-and-soft-reopen-safeguard
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: We observed a pattern where regional failovers during bursty traffic would trigger immediate rejoin attempts and rapid circuit reopen cycles, causing oscillation and degraded SLOs for affected tenants. This PR introduces a regional 'burn-in' stabilizer that performs controlled traffic priming after fallback and applies a soft-reopen safeguard to prevent rapid reopen loops. The change is intended to reduce oscillation, smooth tenant experience during regional failover, and improve SLO stability without hard blocking of traffic.

Change summary (continuous): Adds a burnIn coordinator that tracks per-region priming windows, extends the failover policy to mark fallback candidates as "priming" instead of immediate full-capacity join, implements exponential soft-reopen with jitter to stagger rejoin attempts, and records detailed telemetry for priming windows and reopen decisions. Includes a hotfix for a race in circuit-state persistence that could clear sticky penalties on concurrent evictions. Backwards-compatible config flags added to the routing policy to allow staged rollout and emergency disable.

Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for coordinator state transitions and timer expiry - [x] Integration test covering multi-region failover simulation - [x] Load test run against perf-lab showing 42% reduction in reopen flapping in synthetic burst scenario - [x] Telemetry dashboards and Grafana panel JSON included - [x] Rollout plan documented in PR comments and release notes

Operational notes: Default behavior is off behind a runtime flag `regional_burnin_enabled=false`. On merge we will enable in canary region for 24h, monitor SLO and reopen metrics, then enable globally with a gradual ramp. Emergency disable route is provided (routing-control API) if unexpected regressions appear.

Backward compat and safety: The coordinator writes lightweight markers to existing region metadata table and falls back to former behavior if persistence writes fail. No breaking change to client-facing APIs.

References: related Linear cards ENG-1983 (reduce reopen oscillation) and ENG-1984 (regional priming). Support ticket SUP-7412 contains customer reproduction and logs.

Why unique: Unlike prior efforts that focused on static cooldowns or tenant-level backoff, this PR introduces a region-scoped burn-in window and staggered soft-reopen algorithm that coordinates reopen attempts across nodes to avoid rebuild storms while keeping capacity available incrementally.

b8f1c9d: routing policy: add priming state and soft-reopen config knobs
c4e7f33: fix: race in circuit persistence when eviction and reclaim happen concurrently
d2a1f0b: telemetry: add priming/window events, reopen decision traces, and dashboard JSON
e9b6a55: tests: unit and integration tests for burn-in coordinator and staggered reopen
review_comments: Omar Patel: Please add a short note about how this interacts with tenant-level sticky penalties. Are they additive or superseded?

Maya Chen (author): Sticky penalties remain additive; coordinator marks region-level priming separately and decision logic composes tenant penalty + region priming weight. Added comment and unit tests to clarify behavior.
Linnea Berg: The exponential backoff parameters look aggressive for low-capacity regions. Can we add a per-region multiplier?
Maya Chen (author): Added `region_multiplier` config and conservative defaults. Also included runtime tunable to tweak on canary.
Ravi Kapoor: CI flake on integration test; reran and green. Consider adding small jitter to test timestamps to avoid timing sensitivity.
Maya Chen (author): Added jitter in test harness; reran locally and updated assertions.
release_notes: Introduce a regional burn-in stabilizer that staggers rejoin attempts after fallback and prevents reopen oscillation. Default disabled; gated rollout with runtime flag. Hotfix for circuit persistence race included.
